Amanda — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (security/ops) to propose concrete language and the operational playbook.

Preliminary answers:
- SOC 2 Type II: attached copy (same as the one in your packet) covers our hosted and dedicated offerings; for private deployments we provide an attestation and can arrange a scoped evidence review.
- Pen-test: our standard allowance is a 7–30 day scheduling window depending on environment; we can agree to a minimum 14-day notice for production-facing scans and a 48–72 hour staging access window.
- Evidence cadence: we typically provide quarterly control snapshots for high-risk controls and annual full packages; we can provide a rolling sample set if that helps your audit window.

I've attached an initial set of redlines to the inspection appendix (redlines_inspection_playbook_v1.docx). Laura — could you take the legal redlines below and turn them into contract text? Specific asks I want to protect are: (a) limiting the scope of on-site data extraction, (b) mandatory non-production sandbox for active exploitation tests, and (c) a requirement that Atlas provide a PO/authorization for testing windows.

Marcus

Marcus / Amanda — I reviewed the draft. Below is proposed contract language that legal recommends for the Security Exhibit. Feel free to take this verbatim into redlines; it's intentionally prescriptive to reduce back-and-forth.

Proposed Security Exhibit paragraph (for insertion into the MSA / Order Form):
"Inspection Rights; Penetration Testing. Subject to reasonable advance notice (no fewer than fourteen (14) calendar days for production systems), Customer may conduct or engage a third-party to conduct penetration tests against Redwood-managed interfaces. All testing must be limited to non-production environments unless expressly agreed in writing. Redwood will provide temporary access credentials and a dedicated staging environment for penetration testing; Customer shall not extract production data or perform exploitation leading to data exfiltration. For private/on-prem deployments, Customer may request evidence snapshots and agreed inspection artifacts; Redwood will provide redacted telemetry and control evidence as necessary to protect customer data and Redwood trade secrets. Any access granted under this Section will be governed by a mutually executed Test Authorization (e.g., signed form or DocuSign) that specifies scope, scheduling, and reporting obligations."

Key negotiation points I expect Atlas to flag:
- "Non-production only" vs. limited production testing — we'll likely allow production testing with stricter controls and an indemnity carve-out.
- "Evidence redaction specifics — we'll need to state that Redwood will perform redaction where necessary and provide attestations."

Marcus — please confirm whether we should include a clause on sample-set rotation (we typically offer quarterly snapshots for controls but can do ad-hoc slices for audits with 7 business days' notice).

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Adding the ops perspective — a couple of technical constraints and proposed mitigations: 
- Staging environment provisioning: for dedicated and private installs we need a minimum 48-hour lead time to spin up an isolated staging replica with sanitized data. For hosted tenants we can provide a shared sandbox but will schedule windows to avoid noisy neighbor impact.
- Test authorization metadata: the Test Authorization should require the following: target IP ranges, test types (SAST/DAST/exploit), expected tool signatures, and POC contact. That reduces accidental escalations.
- Evidence snapshots: we can provide quarterly control snapshots; for auditors requesting more frequent samples we'll require a written request and a 5–7 business day turnaround.

Quoted from Laura's proposed paragraph: "Redwood will provide temporary access credentials and a dedicated staging environment for penetration testing; Customer shall not extract production data or perform exploitation leading to data exfiltration." — this is important operationally. For production testing exceptions we need: (1) pre-approved runbook, (2) escrowed rollback playbook, and (3) an on-call Redwood engineer during the window.

I'll prepare a short ops addendum that can sit behind the security exhibit to capture these operational guarantees.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
